attributes.body_ja:
「がち」は名詞（めいし）や動詞（どうし）の連用形（れんようけい）のあとで使（つか）われる接尾語（せつびご）です。「(A) になることが多（おお）い」ことを表（あらわ）します。たいていは悪（わる）いことに使（つか）われますが、そうでないこともあります。

豆知識（まめちしき）

「がち」を漢字（かんじ）で書（か）くと「勝（が）ち」になります。この漢字（かんじ）から、「たくさんある可能性（かのうせい）の中（なか）から、結局（けっきょく） (A) が勝（か）つ（＝ (A) になることが多（おお）い）」というイメージを持（も）つと覚（おぼ）えやすいでしょう。そうなる原因（げんいん）は、その人（ひと）の好（この）みのこともあれば、単（たん）に運（うん）によることもあります。
attributes.body:
がち is a suffix in Japanese that will be used after nouns, or the conjunctive form of verbs. It conveys that someone is 'apt to (A)', 'tends to (A)', or 'is prone to (A)'. Although not always negative, がち is most frequently used to express negative tendencies.

Fun Fact

がち as a grammar structure comes from the word 勝（が）ち, meaning 'a win'. 勝（が）ち in itself is used to express something that appears 'repeatedly', or 'again and again'. Due to this, がち may be thought of as similar to 'to win out' in English, meaning that 'although there are many possibilities, (A) winning out is the most likely'. This 'winning out' may be due to preference, or sheer good/bad luck.

attributes.source: [AIAIJ] An Integrated Approach to Intermediate Japanese

attributes.description: How to use がち and ぎみ

attributes.body: Both express tendencies or patterns of behavior, but they differ in tone and usage. がち attaches to verb stems, and is neutral, used for tendencies that happen often, e.g. つい忘れがちだ ('I tend to forget.'). きらいがある follows the plain form of verbs and is typically used only for undesirable tendencies. Unlike がち, it can also express a tendency to not do something, e.g. 人の話を聞かないきらいがある ('He tends to not listen to others.').

attributes.body: Both がち and っぽい describe tendencies or characteristic qualities, but differ in nuance. がち is neutral and used for tendencies that happen often, e.g. つい忘れがちだ ('I tend to forget.'). っぽい expresses an inherent quality or the appearance of something, similar to the English '~ish', e.g. 子供っぽい性格 ('a childish personality').
